problems: major (stretched clip, the one the edit uses): the motion interpolation breaks the bat during the fast swing. major (raw clip): the ball hangs motionless in mid-air at (255,430) from 0 to 2.29 s and never comes in, even while he swings (1.6-2.29 s). In the stretched clip that is 0-3.2 s of a 4.3 s shot.
minor (raw clip): 0-1.6 s is nearly a still picture (frame-to-frame change ~1 against ~8-15 later), with only slight breathing.

minor-to-major (raw clip): from ~2.17 s he turns square to the camera. Front-on (2.67-3.33 s) the face is harder and older: a frown, heavy brows, a square jaw and a dark chin that reads like stubble. minor (raw clip): the swing is a flat, hip-height sweep. The bat drops behind him to the right at 2.0-2.08 s and sweeps low to the left at 2.33-2.38 s, which reads more like a slog or baseball swing than a cricket drive. The bat finishes up-left at mid height, not high.
notes: Held in the raw clip: the bat is ONE straight piece in every frame, with no V bend. There is one ball only. The swing happens, with a left-handed path (backlift over his left shoulder, through towards the bowler on the left). Painted anime all through, no text, boards blurred, no flicker.
fix: Two parts. (1) Re-time S06 without motion-compensated interpolation (repeat frames, on twos, instead of minterpolate mci) and check it again. That removes the broken bat and the lost ball, keeps this take's clean hit, and lands the contact at about 3.2 s of the 4.3 s shot. (2) For the frozen ball and the face turning to camera, make 2-3 new seeds with a prompt in which the red ball flies in from the left and he keeps his eyes on the ball, side-on, through the follow-through.
